sec: Chylous vs pseudochylous ascites: the table · p1006

items.q: Match the chylous column of the comparative table — 1) Onset 2) Cause 3) Triglycerides 4) Lipoprotein electrophoresis … A) Chylomicrons present B) Sudden C) > 110 mg/dL D) Trauma
items.exp: Chylous: sudden onset, trauma, milky-white (or yellow to bloody), lymphocytosis, triglycerides > 110 mg/dL, chylomicrons present. (Book p1006)

items.q: Match the pseudochylous column of the comparative table — 1) Onset 2) Cause 3) Microscopic examination 4) Appearance … A) Milky or greenish, metallic sheen B) Mixed cellular reaction, cholesterol crystals C) Gradual D) Rheumatoid arthritis / TB
items.exp: Pseudochylous: gradual onset, RA/TB, milky or greenish with metallic sheen, mixed cellular reaction with cholesterol crystals, triglycerides < 50 mg/dL, chylomicrons absent with cholesterol crystals (+) on electrophoresis. (Book p1006)

items.q: In the comparative table, the triglyceride level that defines chylous ascites is:
items.exp: Triglycerides: chylous > 110 mg/dL versus pseudochylous < 50 mg/dL. (Book p1006)

items.q: ‘Pseudochylous ascites shows chylomicrons on lipoprotein electrophoresis.’
opts: False — chylomicrons are absent and cholesterol crystals are (+)
False — pseudochylous shows neither chylomicrons nor crystals
items.exp: Pseudochylous lipoprotein electrophoresis: chylomicrons absent, cholesterol crystals (+). (Book p1006)

items.q: A patient 48 h after an aorto-iliac procedure develops milky-white ascites; the fluid shows lymphocytosis and triglycerides 150 mg/dL. Per this is:
opts: Low-SAAG ascites due to peritoneal CA
items.exp: Sudden onset after trauma, milky-white, lymphocytosis and TG > 110 mg/dL = chylous. (Book p1006)

items.q: The pseudochylous ascitic fluid's characteristic appearance is:
opts: Milky or greenish with a metallic sheen
items.exp: Appearance: chylous — milky-white or yellow to bloody; pseudochylous — milky or greenish, metallic sheen. (Book p1006)
